summary: In a major international civil space development, NASA formally welcomed Albania as the newest signatory to the Artemis Accords, expanding the diplomatic framework for peaceful lunar exploration. On the science front, data from NASA’s Perseverance rover at "Turquoise Bay" revealed that early Mars hosted complex water systems marked by at least three distinct aqueous episodes. In orbital research, student-led missions successfully deployed free-flying light sails from CubeSats in low Earth orbit, while Solar Orbiter detected previously missing high-speed vibrations from the sun. In military space operations, the Space Development Agency announced efforts to expand its ground architecture to support future missile-tracking satellite constellations. Within the commercial sector, Exolaunch booked its first Starfall mission, and the Commercial Space Federation welcomed two new members into its industry group. Domestically, NASA launched a nationwide initiative to prepare the future space workforce while promoting internal policies to treat data, software, and artificial intelligence as strategic assets. Looking ahead, space sector observers should watch for further deployment timelines following the announcement of the joint GHOST-R mission by the Defense Innovation Unit and Space Systems Command.
